title: exceptions.jsonl row (one person's waiver of one stop)
description: One row per stop a person authorised the session to go past, in .dabbler/runs/s<N>/exceptions.jsonl. A rule may be waived and a record may never be falsified: the row keeps the stop exactly as the framework wrote it -- the test failed, no verdict came, the check refused -- and adds that a person authorised going on, and why. It never says the gate was met, and nothing it covers is rewritten. A waiver is of THAT stop, matched on its kind and the time it was written: the next stop, or the same rule refusing a tree that has since moved, needs its own. Written only by the CLI (dabbler session waive), which an engine is refused.

stop.description: The stop waived, copied from run.json as the framework wrote it.

kind.description: The kinds with something to go past. Every other stop has its own way on, and a waiver cannot make a push or a provider answer.

reason.description: What was unmet, in the framework's words.

at.description: When the stop was written; what the loop matches the waiver to.

reason.description: Why the person authorised going on, in their words. Permanent.

by.description: Who was working, as the session record from 'dabbler session start' says; written by the verb and never typed.

commit.description: HEAD when the waiver was given.

tree.description: The worktree snapshot when the waiver was given, so a reader can see which tree was let through. Absent when the snapshot could not be taken.
